response.justification: The candidate is an experienced full-stack/web engineer (13+ years) with strong software craftsmanship, testing, and some low-latency backend work in D, but the resume shows essentially no overlap with the core requirements of this Principal Performance Architect role: no SoC/IP modeling, no hardware-software co-design, no GPU/accelerator architecture, no SIMD/MIMD work, and no deep-learning training/inference optimization. The closest adjacent experience is C/C++ component work at National Instruments and high-throughput microservices at Sociomantic, which is application-level rather than silicon-level performance work. Education is a BS in CS with sufficient years of experience to meet the minimum bar on paper, but the technical domain mismatch is decisive for a principal-level IC hire where deep specialization is expected from day one.
strengths: 13+ years of broad engineering experience, including low-latency, high-throughput systems in D
Some systems/C/C++ exposure (National Instruments LabWindows/CVI, embedded, audio DSP thesis)
Strong engineering discipline and community leadership (TDD, CI/CD, open-source tooling, workshops)
concerns: No SoC/IP modeling, hardware-software co-design, or chip architecture experience
No AI accelerator, GPU architecture, SIMD/MIMD, or DNN training/inference optimization background
Career trajectory is web/full-stack product engineering, not principal-level hardware performance architecture

key_factors.factor: Missing SoC/IP modeling and hardware architecture expertise
No AI/deep-learning workload or accelerator optimization experience
Extensive general software engineering and low-latency systems background
